verdict_question: Does a keyless GET of the public telemetry endpoint return varying measured_us values, and is the reported latency consistent with the measured round-trip time?
probe_title: NEOMA P-CAM telemetry: do repeated public GETs return varying measured_us consistent with the 0.011 ms claim?
one_line: A hobby API claims real analog hardware sits behind every answer; I will hit its public telemetry endpoint and see whether the numbers vary like measurements.

Verdict is plausible, static or fabricated looking, with the limit that hardware cannot be proven remotely.

mechanism: It finds candidate dead code, files, dependencies and assets by name-mention analysis (a name only mentioned in its own definition is dead), deletes them in a batch and runs the user's own test command. If the check fails, the batch is bisected until the breaking cut is found and restored, and tests must not fall in count. Edited files are parsed first, and ambiguous cases go to an agent.
claim: Deletes dead code and keeps each cut only if your tests still pass; 46% fewer tokens to read on its demo app.

needs: npm or cargo and a project with tests
one_line: Shrink-anything deletes dead code in batches and bisects on test failure, so only cuts your own tests accept survive.
idea_why: Delete-then-test with bisection is a safe way to prune, though it is only as strong as the test suite.
breakdown: Install it, run scan on a Proteus sub-project that has tests, then cut with that project's test command. Count lines removed, tests before and after and whether any removed item was actually used. The same loop could be written in about eighty lines of Python for sandbox scripts as a cheaper alternative.
